admission.justification: MIK-R192 rule 6 spans the settings merge, the launch defaults and the host hand-off, each covered by tests in this candidate.

applicability: Every start and resume of a role seat through the host, from harness-level and role-level settings.
conditions: Harness entries follow the harness the start actually uses; only a harness that takes extra command-line arguments in this build receives any.

Role entries lay over the harness entry key by key, and a role entry set to false removes the harness entry of that name; a role entry takes effect only when the start's harness is the role's settings harness, so a start on another harness, or one with no settings harness at all, takes none of them and records why.
Every argument a start takes carries its provenance (harness entry or role entry, with its key), and every entry the start does not take is recorded with its reason rather than silently dropped.
The host's own configured arguments are noted as configuration and never taken; a map that could not be read is recorded as unread, so a clean configuration file is not reported as a clean host.
The arguments are handed to the host per start, user's layer only, and reserved names are refused; a confined capability receives none.

The host keeps the arguments it was given when it created the agent and applies them again when that same agent resumes; AR supplies them at creation and does not re-send them on resume, so a resume runs on the creation arguments the host retains, and a start that takes none takes none on resume either.
exclusions: The explainer and the presenter get none, at any start or resume.
The host leg spawns --chrome only on the developer's word, and which browser an agent uses is not AR's matter.

Settings cleanliness is bounded to what AR declares and provisions and to the confined checks AR controls; a configuration edited outside AR keeps whatever it holds, and that external drift is recorded as a residual rather than claimed controlled.
statement: A role's settings may carry extra harness arguments, laid over the harness entry key by key, with a role entry set to false removing the harness entry, and a confined capability receiving none; role entries are taken only where the start's harness is the role's own settings harness and that harness takes extra arguments in this build, and a start that does not match says so instead of taking them.
